text:
Maria (PM): quick sync — AtlasPay asked for a launch window for their high-throughput payments assistant. They want sub-50ms 95th-token latency for short prompts and strict KV isolation between tenants. We need to decide PRD scope: kernel selection strategy + attention opt + KV cache policy. Thoughts? :wave:

Raj (Eng-runtime): short answer: doable but tradeoffs. sub-50ms 95p on our current L4 stack needs aggressive batching limits + per-tenant cache pinning. If we also require quantized kernels for cost -> some model variants lose exactness.

Sophia (Eng-ML): +1. For short prompts we can use an attention-optimized kernel (reduced attention compute) but that increases variance for longer contexts. Acceptance criteria should call out both short/long behavior. Also need eval prompts from AtlasPay to validate quality regression.

Owen (Product): AtlasPay will only accept rollouts with: (1) documented latency SLOs, (2) deterministic fallback if kernel incompatible, (3) audit logs for cache hits by tenant. They flagged two hard edge cases: cold-start storm during billing close, and large multi-ttoken invoices that hit long-context paths.

Raj (Eng-runtime): proposal: PRD scoped to phased rollout — Phase A: latency-focused kernels + strict KV tenant namespace (no cross-tenant sharing). Phase B: add adaptive kernel switching for mid-latency workloads and prefetch heuristics. Phase C: widen to mixed-tenant caching with TTLs.

Maria (PM): acceptance checklist draft (for Phase A):
- 95th-token latency <= 50ms on our target infra for <128 token requests
- end-to-end throughput measured at 2k qps sustained with 5% tail retries
- KV cache isolation: per-tenant namespace, eviction cannot evict another tenant's entries
- automatic fallback to generic kernel on quantization mismatch, with a visible metric in Console
- integration test harness using AtlasPay prompt set (provided)

Sophia (Eng-ML): add quality gates:
- LM perplexity/token-change <= 3% vs baseline for AtlasPay prompts
- no >1% semantic regression on NER/amount extraction evals

Raj (Eng-runtime): technical edge cases to call out in PRD: cold cache prefill strategy (avoid stampede), KV eviction race on heavy writes, kernel-switch transition for in-flight requests. Example config snippet for policy we discussed:

```yaml
kernel_policy:
  prefer_kernel: "attn_fast_v3"
  fallback_kernel: "attn_safe_v1"
  tenant_cache:
    mode: "pinned" # pinned|shared|ttl
    ttl_ms: 0
    max_entries: 50000
  prefetch:
    enabled: true
    heuristic: "recent-prefix"
    max_prefetch: 4
```

Owen (Product): operation questions: who owns the rollout gates? We need SRE + Eng-runtime signoff and an alert playbook for cache contamination or kernel regression. Also legal wants audit log retention defined.

Maria (PM): owners: Eng-runtime owns runtime changes + kernels, Eng-ML owns quality gates, SRE (oncall) owns rollout & alerting. Legal/Compliance to define retention in parallel. Can we add a canary stage that pins AtlasPay traffic to a dedicated pool?

Raj (Eng-runtime): yes — dedicated pool for canary recommended. Also suggest a steering policy: route by latency SLO + feature flag to force fallback. We'll need a small kernel acceptance test harness (unit + perf) before canary. deploy-bot will run perf bench on PRs.

deploy-bot: perf-bot queued: running attn_fast_v3 vs attn_safe_v1 microbenchmarks on p4d-small. Expected results by EOD. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Sophia (Eng-ML): action items for PRD draft:
- list required datasets from AtlasPay (prompt set + edge cases)
- define quality thresholds and evaluation pipeline
- specify rollback metrics (latency/regression triggers)

Maria (PM): next steps: I'll draft PRD with phased scope and owners, include Raj's config examples and Sophia's quality gates. Tagging @Raj and @Sophia for review. Please add notes on any missing edge cases — especially multi-tenant QoS interference and legal retention windows. :rocket:
